parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile at every journey stage. The interior ministry may refuse entry or remove travellers perceived as queer with no charge or conviction (12 documented incidents, 2018–2022) — a state-directed, visitor-facing exposure. Vague morality/public-immorality provisions carry prison sentences (current as of March 2026), and police run app-based entrapment specifically targeting transgender women, with blackmail, arrests, custody abuse and coerced anal examinations documented. No anti-discrimination law exists; legal gender recognition is being actively closed; courts read morality statutes expansively rather than restraining police. Removal requiring no offence makes outing consequential by design. No execution is documented, and the worst custody-abuse incidents date to 2017 with removals to 2022, so severity sits at imprisonment-plus-abuse rather than the extreme endpoint.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior ministry may deny entry or order removal of anyone 'disturbing public order or morality'; 12 documented incidents 2018–2022 applied to travellers perceived as queer, some deported with no charge ever upheld. Removal needs neither conviction nor offence.
entry_documents.protection: No documented protection: no charge required, no trans-specific entry screening protocol recorded either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Document or presentation mismatch during routine checks feeds straight into the removal power with no judicial gate documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police run entrapment via fake accounts on LGBT dating apps, transgender women named as particular targets; blackmail and arrests reported. Vague morality laws yield prison sentences; documented physical abuse and coerced anal examinations in custody; violations continue inside police stations.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Only a dated 2014 raid ending in acquittal; no current remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: App encounter → arrest → custody abuse; entrapment manufacture converts ordinary online activity into prosecutable conduct.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No prison, ward or facility placement rule for trans visitors appears in the dossier.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A uniform nationwide ministry directive shows enforcement reach is centralised, so any future placement rule would apply across all provinces.

care_services.exposure: Gender-identity and sexual-orientation discrimination in healthcare described as pervasive and persistent across review cycles (January 2025 submission), violating the right to health.
care_services.protection: None documented; no anti-discrimination law covers services.
care_services.interaction: An outed visitor needing emergency or routine care encounters the same documented barriers as residents, with no complaint route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police as perpetrators via entrapment and station-level violations; media incitement (2017 flag incident, doxxing of participants); a stigmatising label applied to gender-nonconforming men; an undated survey cited at 95% societal non-acceptance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; parties and NGOs do not publicly support LGBT rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Media exposure converts visibility into arrest lists, feeding the removal and prosecution powers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. A minor accompanying an outed parent would enter the same removal and morality-law regime, but no age-specific rule or incident appears.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent's outing plausibly exposes the accompanying child to removal and social hostility; this is extrapolation, not dossier fact.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National policing pattern of app-based entrapment, blackmail, arrests of gay and trans people, coerced examinations, authorities turning a blind eye; documented arrest surges after visibility events.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; no hate-crime or identity-based protection exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street and online encounter routes directly into custody where abuse is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute; removal without charge; courts expand morality/sex-work provisions (de facto to explicit criminalisation, 2024); undated hostility figure and undated app-entrapment sources; unresolved legal effect of the December 2024 directive.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Only dated acquittals (2014 raid) and visibility campaigns that produced no legal reform.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Institutional machinery operates against, not for, trans people — efficient enforcement of hostile rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A (Vellandra's exclusion register): that anchor stops at refusal and humiliation with no charge. Here removal coexists with criminal prosecution under prison-carrying morality laws, state-run entrapment targeting trans women, and documented custody abuse — a materially more severe consequence set after discovery.

Close to 0.15-B (Saruth): border removal aimed at trans visitors, custody abuse, and remedies that fail are shared. Slightly above it because no capital provision is documented anywhere in this dossier, and the worst custody/forced-examination incidents are dated (2017) with removals to 2022, leaving severity at imprisonment-plus-abuse rather than quasi-capital uncertainty.

Below 0.25-C (Ostravia): there the state's reach is a cross-dressing statute plus birth-sex housing with courts recognising safety in principle. Here the state itself manufactures cases through app entrapment, removes travellers without charge, and has no anti-discrimination or recognition recourse at all — worse than slow-but-restraining courts.

parsed.synthesis: The exposure chain is unusually complete for a visitor: discovery is engineered (app entrapment naming transgender women, media doxxing, routine document scrutiny feeding a no-charge removal power), and the consequences after discovery are state-imposed at three levels — removal without any offence, prosecution under vague morality provisions carrying prison sentences, and custody where abuse and coerced examinations are documented. Every institution in the record enforces the hostile rule rather than restraining it: courts broaden the statutes, the ministry closes recognition loopholes, police run the entrapment, and no anti-discrimination law exists. Datedness softens but does not reverse this: current (2026) sources still record arrests under these provisions, while only the most brutal custody incidents are old. No execution and no trans-specific entry-screening protocol are documented, keeping the score above the lowest anchors.
